messages.text: Is it quiet enough to run in my office?

**Yes — it's genuinely desk-friendly.**

- **~40–45 dB** at full speed (quiet-room level — think a soft fan, not a jet)
- **0.5 kg, ~20 × 11 × 6 cm** — palm-sized on its stand
- **~100 W** draw — no more heat than a bright light bulb
- ASIC sits at **~57 °C** at full load, so the fan doesn't have to scream to keep up

The spring-mounted heatsink presses evenly on all four chips, and the BSB shroud directs airflow onto the voltage regulators — so it stays cool *quietly*, not by brute-force fan speed.

Most owners run it on a desk or shelf without complaints. Not silent, but easily office-compatible.
Will a power spike fry the whole miner?

**No — there's a dedicated onboard fuse (F1) that takes the hit first.**

- The **F1 fuse sits right on the board**, beside the yellow XT30 power input
- If a spike hits, **F1 blows — not your electronics**
- Replace a cheap automotive-style blade fuse, not a $249 miner

On top of that, the **MEANWELL LRS-350-12 PSU** (included) is a robust industrial supply loafing at ~30% of its 350 W cap···· — it's not a stressed cheap brick that can itself become the problem.

Cheaper miners skip the onboard fuse entirely. A spike there cooks the whole board. Here it costs you a fuse.
